rankings.rank_justification: Opens instantly with cold brutality on 'You were never my Duchess,' escalating without dead air through rapid-fire repudiation until Alexander walks away to favor a shackled woman. The final extreme close-up cut on Catherine's horrified 'Her?!' creates an unbeatable curiosity gap and maximum humiliation payoff.

Kicks off with explosive entitlement and high physical stakes as Catherine shrieks 'I was supposed to be your Duchess,' followed by a sharp verbal confrontation. Cutting on Catherine's horrified gasp of 'Her?!' as the Duke chooses a woman in chains provides peak irresolution and public humiliation.

Arrests swiping attention immediately with the shocking repudiation line, moving through tense emotional friction. The exit visual of Alexander turning his back to approach a chained woman is a compelling visual cliffhanger, though slightly less punctual than cutting directly on Catherine's horrified reaction.

Starts with chaotic physical action and shouting guards that arrests the thumb, building steadily through Catherine's plea to the sharp gut-punch of 'You were never my Duchess.' The final beat lands with immense finality and high irresolution, though the middle mourning beats slightly slow the pacing.

Features a strong, chaotic physical hook and clear emotional stakes as Alexander coldly calls Catherine out as a title-chaser. The cliffhanger on Alexander's set, scarred jaw creates solid curiosity, though extended dialogue beats dilute some of the forward momentum.

Opens on an emotional narrative revelation that requires 2–3 seconds to establish context rather than immediate visual shock. However, it escalates smoothly into Alexander's devastating repudiation cut, leaving the viewer desperate to know the truth behind the broken engagement.

Combines a violent apprehension hook with an escalating argument culminating in Catherine's shout of 'I was supposed to be your Duchess!' While ending on an unresolved demand, it cuts right before Alexander delivers his verbal blow, leaving tension somewhat suspended rather than peaked.

The shouting and guard takedown creates an instant hook, but the middle section lingers on repetitive mourning lines. Alexander's physical flinch and Catherine's trembling hand offer a poignant emotional cliffhanger, though it lacks the explosive stakes of later beats.

Possesses a strong visual and auditory hook with armed redcoats pinning Rupert, but stretching to 50 seconds introduces noticeable mid-clip dialogue plateaus. Alexander's piercing 'Did you?' is a sharp exit, though the long runtime reduces short-form conversion punch.

Strong initial thumb-stop with physical scuffling in the ruined nave, but pacing drags across multiple repetitive romantic assertions. Ending on Catherine rendered speechless defuses active tension into passive silence rather than driving an urgent next-episode swipe.

Strong chaotic hook with guards wrestling Rupert, but quickly decelerates into a sentimental romantic confession ('I never stopped loving you'). Cutting on an unreturned caress feels like a soft pause rather than a high-stakes cliffhanger rupture.
